problem_text:
A logistics company must select packages to load onto a cargo plane. Available packages are:
* Package 1: volume 46 cubic meters, revenue $108
* Package 2: volume 2 cubic meters, revenue $202
* Package 3: volume 22 cubic meters, revenue $145
* Package 4: volume 23 cubic meters, revenue $139
* Package 5: volume 29 cubic meters, revenue $275
* Package 6: volume 48 cubic meters, revenue $29
* Package 7: volume 20 cubic meters, revenue $238
* Package 8: volume 28 cubic meters, revenue $124
* Package 9: volume 49 cubic meters, revenue $252
* Package 10: volume 1 cubic meter, revenue $277
* Package 11: volume 39 cubic meters, revenue $212
* Package 12: volume 46 cubic meters, revenue $182
* Package 13: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue $298
* Package 14: volume 23 cubic meters, revenue $160
* Package 15: volume 11 cubic meters, revenue $100
* Package 16: volume 47 cubic meters, revenue $153
* Package 17: volume 13 cubic meters, revenue $70
* Package 18: volume 23 cubic meters, revenue $203
* Package 19: volume 10 cubic meters, revenue $164
* Package 20: volume 17 cubic meters, revenue $95
* Package 21: volume 26 cubic meters, revenue $24
* Package 22: volume 43 cubic meters, revenue $49

The aircraft's cargo hold has a maximum capacity of 406 cubic meters. Choose the package combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each package must be either fully loaded or left behind.
